questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The process ended up beeing a little bit random because of the COVID restricitions, three of the universities didnt allow exchange students because of restricitions. So Mannheim University hospital (UMM) ended up beeing the last feasable option for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Keeping track of all my email was key. It was unproblematic to get all the information i needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Received assistance via email and at the hospital where i did my clinical rotation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The email service worked well, i had all the information i needed online.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Had to look for a while. after a few hours and unsucsesfull applications on "WG gesucht" i found an email adress that led me to a private person. Got lucky. But would reccomend WG gesucht and start relatively early (2-3 months in advance)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be as good as living on campus. Depends what your preference is in terms of contact with other people, location etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I turned down the Erasmus offer which probably is the easiest way yo get housing on campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite easy and the coordinator was very helpful and friendly. Just follow her steps and ask if it doesnt make any sense!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A Coordinatior that helped making sense of everything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very much successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Explore the oppurtinity for taking some of the classes that your interested in. Maybe you can do cooler things than you believed, it worth giving it a shot ;)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Could have been more structured and student centered. You are the only person that knows what you need to learn, would have been nice with some coordinatiors that could have been a little more available in guiding how to maximize what you get out of the clinical rotation.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Clinical rotations in surgery (vascular surgery + intermidiate care surgical unit), Internal medicine (kardio + gastro) and anesthesiology.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Clinical courses here at UMM, so hard to compare with the theoretical ones in DK.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Clinical rotations in surgery (vascular surgery + intermidiate care surgical unit), Internal medicine (kardio + gastro) and anesthesiology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try to get down to the emergency ward, there is a lot of hands on and interesting diagnostics taking place. You get a much higher flow of patients that need diagnosis!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I believe the non-academic opportunities were really good, however i did not take advantage of them and instead found a soccer team and fitness club that didnt have anything to do with the school

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many, you can find an overview on the university home page.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore some new things and get to et as soon as possible. its great way to build a social network and find friends!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Heidelberg as good train connections to frankfurt, Paris, stuttgart, freiburg, munchen etc etc. Also the Heidelberg area is beautiful and should be explored.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy, im german myself.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open, take initiativ and tell them your from Denmark (the find that intereseting). For me, being abroad is like a holiday, and i try to be curious and open minded about most things. If you have a place to stay, invite them to your home and share food. Germans are more open and spontanious than scandinavians, its easier to get friends!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The german Conservative, hierarchical hospital system.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The spontaneous, open and direct why. Also, Germany has a rich history of great musicians, authors, and art directors.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Depends what person you are and what you need. But this is some general advice.
- find a cool place to stay and start looking relatively early
- Be curious and open, take some chances (both inside and outside of the hospital)
- engage in som extra curricular activities - its good to have some hobbies that one enjoys ;)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting som many interesting people, escpecially at the hospital. Smoking a cigarette during a night shift with a senior doctor, reflecting around what it means to be a doctors. Drinking coffee with the nurses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At times, being on your own to feet, away from familiy and friends (the secure, the know)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
